subject: validate() Inside of tryCatch(), Possible XSS Vulnerability with textInput?

messages.author: de0353bdfec15530
messages.subject: validate() Inside of tryCatch(), Possible XSS Vulnerability with textInput?
parts:
Hi.

I have a Shiny app where the user writes code defining a function they'd like to use to compute distance between data points.  The user inputs the function code in a textInput.  Obviously, allowing the user to write code to execute in the app creates a potential host of problems.  There are many different error / warning messages which can be generated based on the text that the user decides to enter in the textInput.  The solution I had in mind was:

output$plot = renderPlot({

...

custom = tryCatch({
             source(textConnection(isolate(input$customDistanceFunction)))$value
         }, warning = function(w) {
             validate(need(1==2, 'Invalid custom distance function.'))
         }, error = function(e) {
             validate(need(1==2, 'Invalid custom distance function.'))
         }, finally = {
         })

...

})

where custom is the variable that I want to assign the function code to and input$customDistanceFunction is the textInput containing the actual function code (e.g. function(x) { as.dist(t(cor(x))) } ).  If a warning or error message is generated from the source command, I was hoping that the validate(need(1==2, 'Invalid custom distance function.')) calls would always execute and return an error message to the user.  However, this does not seem to be the case, and I've tried putting browser() statements inside of the warning and error functions to try stepping through and figure out why they don't execute, but the code doesn't break inside of the function definitions.

The other thing I'm wondering is whether allowing this sort of code execution by the user could open up security holes in the way of XSS.  If so, I need to learn more about this and any recommended practices for closing these security holes.

Any help would be appreciated.  Thanks!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: validate() Inside of tryCatch(), Possible XSS Vulnerability with textInput?
parts:
First of all, calling source() on user input is absolutely a security hole. There is almost never a reason to do this, unless the app is only meant to be run privately on the end user's own machine (i.e. they're causing code to be executed that they themselves could have executed anyway, as the same user). People may recommend whitelisting or blacklisting certain functions, but such efforts are really really difficult to get right and I would mostly recommend you not go there.

Are the set of possible distance functions so great that it's unfeasible to list them all and let the user choose one of them?

Second, calling source() on a file that contains a function definition will just define the function, it won't actually invoke it. What would the value of the "x" parameter be?

messages.author: de0353bdfec15530
messages.subject: Re: validate() Inside of tryCatch(), Possible XSS Vulnerability with textInput?
parts:
Thanks Joe and Dean.  I had a feeling that this was a major security vulnerability. 

The "x" parameter is a matrix of effect sizes for brain regions and mouse models.  heatmap.2 from the gplots package is then called using the "custom" distance function defined by the user.

I think I'm just going to restrict the possible distance functions to only the most popular ones as per your suggestion Joe.
